markdown.markdown:
Last semester you learned to take a tissue, get counts, and produce a ranked gene list. That is a real skill.

This course is about the layer above it: **being able to tell when an omics result is wrong.**

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Two kinds of depth, and which one this course teaches

**Execution depth** — tuning a doublet detector, building an LD reference panel, implementing spot deconvolution. That is a full-time job, and it belongs to your bioinformatician.

**Judgment depth** — is n = 3 patients or 30,000 cells the real n? Was this polygenic score built on people like my patients? Does this UMAP support the sentence next to it? Would this change what I do on Monday?

→ This course lives on the second. Code appears so that you can **read it and doubt it**, not so that you maintain it.

❌ It does not promise that you will run a spatial deconvolution pipeline unsupervised after fourteen sessions.\
✅ It does promise that you will never again be the person in the room who cannot evaluate the analysis their own name will appear on.
:::

## What you should be able to do in December

-   ✅ Read a methods section and say **what was actually done**, including what was quietly not done
-   ✅ Check whether public data already answers your question, before writing a grant to generate it
-   ✅ Sit in a study-design meeting and stop an unrecoverable mistake
-   ✅ Say why a published finding might not hold in Korean patients
-   ✅ Present a data-supported research proposal at the final session

## Syllabus

| Module | Week | Contents | Key tools |
|-----------------|--------|--------------------------|------------------|
| **Intro** | [W1](chapters/part1/w1_intro.qmd) | Review, roadmap, study design before any data exists | R, Bioconductor |
|  | [W2](chapters/part1/w2_scripts_ai.qmd) | R scripts, AI-assisted coding, reproducibility | Quarto, git |
| **Clinical Genomics** | [W3](chapters/part2/w3_gwas.qmd) | GWAS & post-GWAS | GWAS Catalog, Open Targets |
|  | [W4](chapters/part2/w4_prs.qmd) | Polygenic risk scores & clinical application | PGS Catalog, PRSice-2 |
| **Single-cell** | [W5](chapters/part3/w5_scrna_qc.qmd) | scRNA-seq technology, QC, clustering | Seurat, scanpy |
|  | [W6](chapters/part3/w6_scrna_dynamics.qmd) | Trajectory, cell–cell communication, integration | Monocle3, CellChat, Harmony |
| **Spatial** | [W7](chapters/part4/w7_spatial_basics.qmd) | Spatial transcriptomics — the basics | Seurat, Squidpy |
|  | [W8](chapters/part4/w8_spatial_integration.qmd) | Deconvolution & spatial integration | RCTD, cell2location, CARD |
| **Proteomics** | [W9](chapters/part5/w9_proteomics_tech.qmd) | How proteins are actually measured | MS, Olink, SomaScan |
|  | [W10](chapters/part5/w10_clinical_proteomics.qmd) | Clinical proteomics & biomarkers | limma, MSstats |
| **Integration** | [W11](chapters/part6/w11_multiomics.qmd) | Multi-omics integration | MOFA+, mixOmics |
|  | [W12](chapters/part6/w12_network_drug.qmd) | Network analysis & drug targets | STRING, igraph, Open Targets |
| **Capstone** | [W13](chapters/part7/w13_visualization.qmd) | Interpretation & visualisation | ggplot2, clusterProfiler |
|  | [W14](chapters/part7/w14_project_design.qmd) | Designing your own project | — |

## How each chapter is built

Every week follows the same shape, so you know where to look:

-   🎯 **Learning objectives** — what you should be able to do afterwards
-   🤔 **Motivating question** — a clinical situation, answered by the end of the chapter
-   ⚠️ **Warnings** — the specific ways this method misleads people, marked throughout
-   💻 **Hands-on** — usually starting with a browser exercise that needs no code
-   📝 **Summary** · 🔑 **Key terms** · ➕ **References**

💡 Sections marked ⚠️ are the ones worth reading twice. They are where results go wrong quietly.

## Practice data

The hands-on code loads a handful of datasets. They are **not in this repository** —
download `rawdata.zip` from the course link and unzip it at the top level of your
project, next to your `.Rproj` file.

| Source | Files | Weeks |
|--------------------|-----------------------------|--------------|
| Simulated | `prs_scores.tsv`, `plasma_proteomics.rds`, `plasma_meta.rds` | W4, W10 |
| Real, public | `t2d_gwas_summary.tsv`, `pubmed_counts.rds` | W3, W12 |
| Package data | `pbmc3k`, `stxBrain` — `SeuratData` fetches these for you | W5, W7 |
| You make it | `analysis/5_pbmc_annotated.rds`, `analysis/7_visium.rds` | W5 → W6, W8 |

⚠️ The simulated files are simulated because individual genotypes and patient
specimens cannot be shared. They are **not random noise** — each one has the
phenomenon that week teaches deliberately built into it, and the figures in the
chapters were drawn from these exact files. The headers of
`scripts/make_simulated_data.R` and `scripts/download_public_data.R` document
what each file contains and how it was produced.

💡 Both generator scripts are in `scripts/` and run on base R with no dependencies,
so you can regenerate or modify everything yourself.

## Before the first session

```{r}
install.packages(c("tidyverse", "BiocManager", "here", "renv"))
BiocManager::install(c("DESeq2", "SingleR", "celldex"))
```

Bring one disease you actually treat. We use it throughout.
